## Heading two

A ~~struck~~ word and a "quoted" phrase. The build tests read this paragraph back
out of `dist/` to confirm the Markdown body really is rendered into the page.

### 入れ子の見出し

One level below the heading above it, so the generated contents has a nesting step
to show. The id is the heading text unchanged -- plain Japanese, with no punctuation
for github-slugger to strip -- which is what lets the expected value in
test/build/output.test.ts be read straight off this file.

## 日本語の見出し

Back out to depth 2, so the contents has two top-level entries whose order an
assertion can tell apart. Two entries is also the floor src/lib/toc.ts applies: this
post clears it, and the 2026/08/02 fixture is the one that does not.

# Body heading one

A level-1 heading in the body, which the contents leaves out: `<article>` already
opens with the post title as its h1, so this one is the title's sibling rather than
one of the title's sections. The clash is deliberate and not hypothetical -- the
published post at /posts/2026/09/27/142621/ carries a body h1 exactly like it.

#### Depth four

A level-4 heading, which the contents leaves out as well -- from h4 down a heading is
no longer a landmark worth a line in a bar a fraction of the body's width.

The h1 and the h4 above are test fixtures, not decoration -- do not remove them. They
are the only evidence in `dist/` that the contents selects on depth: without them, a
build that listed every heading it found would be indistinguishable from one that
listed only h2 and h3. The order of these five headings is part of the assertion too,
because a table of contents is a nested, ordered list and is pinned as one.
